observations: 1. Dispatch's thin-slicing observation, measured. The slice file .mob/records/227/turn-slice-architect.md is 55,316 bytes (wc -c): 26,003 the first slice, 13,129 the security review, 16,184 the amendment (awk by line range). The 227-slice window ran 12 min 28 s (opened_at 10:00:35Z to ended_at 10:13:03Z in .mob/records/decisions/227-slice.json) with 7 replies and 6 recorded bad first attempts (each noted 'vote word instead of the window line' and re-polled); 3 of the 7 replies say they did not read the file (product manager ready: 'did not open the slice or card files'; QA engineer: 'only read the first 2KB'; delivery lead: 'didn't open the slice file'). The five earlier slice windows on the record (208, 209, 214, 219, 226 trails, same command) ran 4:05, 4:44, 2:56, 4:02 and 3:09 with 12 replies each and 0 to 1 bad first attempts, on slice files of 24,387, 16,089, 14,588, 14,037 and 18,134 bytes. Per reply that is 1 min 47 s against 15 to 24 s. Time to first red: slice commit 4037cfe (02:43:51 -07:00) to red 524171f (03:24:03) is 40 min 12 s; amendment 2e2e0f3 to window end 17 min 23 s; red seat 10:15:06Z to the red commit 8 min 57 s. Red to green was 48 min 54 s (03:24:03 to 04:12:57), of which the suite 22 min 45 s (1365.4 s) and the rest 26 min 9 s; card 226 criterion 2 was 47 min 58 s, criterion 1 36 min 52 s. Confound that stops me calling it cause: the 227 windows are the first slice windows run one voter at a time through the card 226 decision-seat gate (7 voters, each its own probe and launch), the earlier five were not, so the per-reply time is not comparable and the six re-polls may be the gate and the prompt, not the size.

2. Criterion 1 was closed as 'green' with part of its slice undone. The slice's commit plan puts items 2 (red 1b: FAKE_CLI transcript mode and the decider voter case), 5 (command_source.py), 7 (run_backend session id, scan_out, CardRun Safety flag, decider command_scan field) and 8 (check_record requires command_scans) in criterion 1; the red says 'Not in this red (red 1b and later)' and the green says 'run_backend is not yet wired'; git shows 2 commits for criterion 1 (233 and 363 lines) against 8 planned (about 1,200 lines). What exists: scan_command and the scan-transcript CLI with exit 0, 1 or 2 (the test of the card 226 slip and the Zero case). What does not: nothing calls the CLI from facilitator.py or decider.py and no record check fails an unscanned seat, so as of 2fc4f98 F-071 is closed in the test and open in practice. Whether the board's Done check 1 (a transcript or hook source) is met by the CLI alone, or the slice's wider wording applies, is a question for the team; it is not decided anywhere in the record.

3. Facilitator turn handling: the facilitator's note reconciles bounded turns and never idling mid-card (a turn ends only after a capped wait shows progress). Git evidence: seat result 2fc4f98 (04:12:57) to the facilitator's record commit de575ce (04:13:54) is 57 s; between the green seat's wait line c7cafe1 (03:48:56) and the next commit 2bd233e (04:01:29) there are 12 min 33 s with no commit, which fits a blocking wait and an idle turn equally; turn endings leave no commit: not measured.

4. Probe cadence: the rows at 08:39:31, 09:34:31, 10:26:26 and 11:01:24 UTC are 55 min 0 s, 51 min 55 s and 34 min 58 s apart; 2 of 3 gaps are over the 50 minutes card 226's stand-down 1 asked for, but no seat started on a probe older than 40 min 35 s (the red seat at 10:15:06), so the 60-minute stale limit never came near (card 226: gaps of 49 min 54 s and 29 min). One of the two is already deviation 4.

5. The 52 lines matching rm -rf, rmtree or Remove-Item -Recurse in the added lines of mob-defaults 56b39bc..2fc4f98 (grep -c) are test inputs and the scan code's own patterns, as the bodies say (strings only, nothing run); recursive deletes executed by a seat since 08:30 UTC: 0 found by the new scan in 97 of 97 transcripts (see the D166 review); seat briefs repeating the delete rule: not measured (briefs are not in git).

THIN-SLICING VERDICT (the team decides). Adopt as this stand-down's one adjustment: no. For: the signal is real and measured in git and the trail: 55,316 bytes against 14 to 24 KB for the five earlier slices, 3 of 7 voters did not read the file, the window ran 12 min 28 s against 3 to 5, the criterion 1 cycle took 48.9 minutes of which 22.8 is the suite and 26.1 the rest, and criterion 1 was in effect already sliced thin in execution (2 of 8 planned commits) with the rest dropped quietly. Against adopting it now: (1) confounded, the 227 windows are the first through the one-at-a-time gate with a probe per voter, so the 6 re-polls and the per-reply time are not shown to come from size, and n is 1 card; (2) the stated counter-metric 'count of follow-up cards' is the wrong guard, because filing a card is cheap and a drop in the number proves nothing, while a rise could mean good slicing; (3) the hypothesis as worded (cut each vote window and time-to-first-red) skips the cost that criterion 1 showed: thin slicing without accounting leaves items undone, which my adjustment targets first. Verdict on the hypothesis: half supported. Supported: size raised the cost of reading (voters not reading, 3 of 7). Not shown: that size caused the window time or the 40 minutes to first red (the confound above, and 12 of those 40 minutes were the amendment the security review required, which a thinner slice would also have needed). Suggested test for the retro, not adopted here: the slice for the next card with a slice (card 228 or the next ranked card) is one file per criterion, none over about 20 KB (the largest of the five before 227 was 24 KB), with the measures re-taken by the same commands: slice window minutes, voters saying they did not read (baseline 3 of 7) and slice commit to first red (baseline 40 min 12 s); counter-metrics: plan items undone at a closed criterion (baseline 4) and follow-up cards filed, read only together with the first, since it is no guard on its own.
